name: Kegety Waterfall
near: Kegety dachas (~4.5 km as the crow flies) and Kegety village at the mouth of the gorge; Tokmok — ~20 km to the gorge, Bishkek — 70–85 km (too.kg, hiking.kg).
elev: Drop height — about 30 m (too.kg). The absolute elevation above sea level is not confirmed: the gorge starts at ~1250 m and rises to a pass at ~4000 m (too.kg); the waterfall is in the lower-middle part, roughly 1800–2000 m (estimate, to be verified).
short: The first (big) waterfall of the Kegety gorge — a full-flowing stream about 30 m high, 200 m from the road, 2 hours' drive from Bishkek.
desc: Kegety Waterfall is the most accessible and best-known of several waterfalls in the Kegety gorge on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Range. Too.kg describes it as a “small but full-flowing” stream about 30 m high with cold, clean water. It falls from a sheer rock face 200 m from the dirt road through the gorge — about 5 minutes on foot, ~30 m of ascent (hiking.kg). Opposite the waterfall in summer there are yurts serving food; further up the gorge is the branch to Lake Kol-Tor and trails to the upper waterfalls. The gorge stretches for ~27 km (too.kg); it is popular for day trips and picnics from Bishkek.
guide: Kegety Waterfall is an easy half-day target: the car stops almost at the foot, and 5 minutes on foot puts you in the spray of a 30 m stream. Come in the first half of the day: the sun lights up the jet and a rainbow sometimes forms above it. If you have more energy, climb the steep path above the waterfall to the viewpoints, or combine it with a hike to Kol-Tor (the fork is lower down the gorge). In summer there are yurts opposite the waterfall where you can have lunch. The rocks by the water are wet and slippery — shoes with good soles are a must.
see: The waterfall itself (~30 m) and the basin beneath it; viewpoints above the waterfall along the steep path; in winter, a partly frozen waterfall (video); in the gorge, the upper waterfalls, the Kol-Tor valley and yurts on the meadows.
skip: You're looking for a big, powerful waterfall — this one is modest (about 30 m), and hiking.kg rates the place 6/10. You don't want to drive 2+ hours for a 5-minute walk — then combine it with Kol-Tor or Burana. You have no car — public transport goes only as far as the village.
diff: Easy: 200 m from the road, ~5 min, ~30 m of ascent (hiking.kg). The climb above the waterfall is a separate steep section.
when: May to September: the road is dry, the water is fullest in late spring to early summer (snowmelt), and the yurts are open (too.kg). In winter the waterfall partly freezes and is photogenic too, but the dirt road may be covered in snow and ice (video of a winter visit; editorial).
hours: Google Maps, viewed 03.10.2026: Daily: open 24 hours. Check separately the ticket office hours and access to the routes.
daytime: Hiking.kg recommends the first half of the day for the light on the waterfall.
how: Via Krasnaya Rechka, Yuryevka, Syn-Tash and Rot-Front to Kegety. After the first bridge, at the fork, go right to the next bridge, then left, and about 5 km along the gorge.
needcar: Yes: a car or a tour. The marshrutka (minibus) from Bishkek's Eastern Bus Station goes only as far as Kegety village (thegonegoat, asia-hikes); from there it's ~5 km up the gorge on foot or by hitching a ride.
self: Yes: no permits needed, the waterfall is by the road. At the entrance to the gorge there is a post charging an eco fee per car.
roadtype: Paved road on the approach gives way to a dirt road; a short path leads to the waterfall.
traveltime: Hiking.kg: 85 km / 2 h 15 min from Bishkek; from the road about 200 m / 5 minutes on foot, ascent about 30 m.
stay: Yurts opposite the first waterfall with meals; a small hotel beyond the first barrier; a guesthouse in the Kol-Tor tract with full board (too.kg); Kegety Tour guesthouse — 1500 som/person with three meals a day (asia-hikes). Names of the yurt camps and 2026 prices are not confirmed.
net: Too.kg describes a signal in the lower part of Kegety up to the first waterfall; above that it becomes unstable. The operator and date of measurement are not stated.
entry: About 200 som per car at the Kegety post according to Hiking.kg for 2024; the current fee as of 04.10.2026 is not confirmed.
transfer: Not confirmed: no current taxi/transfer prices from Bishkek were found. For reference: the Trekking Union tour to Kol-Tor ~450 som/person (2024), marshrutka to Kegety 50 som (2024, probably outdated).
bring: Shoes with non-slip soles; poles for the steep path above the waterfall.
warn: Wet, slippery rocks at the base of the waterfall — don't go close to the jet and don't climb the rocks. After rains and during floods the road through the gorge turns to mud; on the upper sections you need a 4×4 / SUV (too.kg). Don't drink river water untreated — livestock graze above (too.kg). The signal disappears above the waterfall.
food: In summer — yurts with food opposite the first waterfall (too.kg): usually Kyrgyz home cooking, tea, kumys (editorial; menu not confirmed). There are practically no shops in the gorge — it's better to buy food in Tokmok or Ivanovka.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 682 ratings/reviews according to the listing counter on 03.10.2026. Review texts were not used to confirm prices, roads or safety.
p.sum: The waterfall is an easy half-day target: the car drives almost to the foot, ≈200 m (5 min) from the road. Route from Bishkek (≈85 km, 2 h 15 min): Krasnaya Rechka — Yuryevka — Syn-Tash — Rot-Front — Kegety village, after the first bridge go right, after the next bridge left, and ≈5 km along the gorge; the first ~10 km of the gorge are passable by an ordinary car. Without a car — marshrutka (minibus) No. 303 from the Eastern Bus Station to Kegety (09:30/15:30, ≈80 som) and 5 km on foot/by hitching, or a tour (Sputnik8 $200–300 per car together with Burana). In summer there are yurts with food opposite the waterfall; it's best combined with Kol-Tor or Burana.

p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Kegety + Kol-Tor (the same gorge); + Burana (via Tokmok); + Boom Gorge/Konorchek on the way to Issyk-Kul.
p.season: Late May–June: full water from snowmelt, the most powerful flow. July–September: dry road, yurts open. October: cold, few people. November–April: the waterfall partly freezes, the dirt road is covered in snow/ice.
p.budget.economy: ≈500–1000 som/person: marshrutka No. 303 2×80 som + 5 km on foot/hitching, food 300–500 som in a yurt.
p.budget.comfort: ≈3000–8000 som/person: taxi ≈1500 som one way per car, or a Sputnik8 tour $200–300 per car with Burana.
p.permits: Not needed. Eco fee at the post at the gorge entrance ≈200 som per car (hiking.kg 2024; not confirmed for 2026 — keep cash).
p.access: With children — yes (200 m from the road, watch them on wet rocks). Older people — yes, with care. Stroller — the path is narrow and rocky, partly. With a dog — yes.
